Alabama Crimson Tide.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Alabama Crimson Tide.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Alabama Crimson Tide.offensive_scheme: RPO. The guide states DeBoer and coordinator Ryan Grubb want to run an RPO offense, and that Keelon Russell suits it.
Alabama Crimson Tide.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated tendency. The guide records that the 2025 run game was the core problem at 3.4 yards per carry and 104 rushing yards per game, and calls restoring balance a priority.
Alabama Crimson Tide.qb_development: Explicitly credited. The guide treats DeBoer's record of developing quarterbacks as making Keelon Russell a safe bet to be what people expect.
Alabama Crimson Tide.continuity: High at coordinator level: head coach, offensive coordinator and defensive coordinator all return, with only the quarterback changing.
Alabama Crimson Tide.portal_recruiting: Not addressed in guide as a staff-driven effect.
Alabama Crimson Tide.vsin_assessment: The guide's framing question is whether DeBoer can meet the fanbase's expectations, and its answer is conditional: if the offense clicks, this roster has the pieces for DeBoer's first national title.
Alabama Crimson Tide.strengths: A stated record of developing quarterbacks, a returning coordinator pair, and a defense expected to be about as productive as last season with seven starters back.
Alabama Crimson Tide.concerns: The offense has to be rebuilt after heavy departures, and the guide's doubts about the team sit entirely on that side.
Alabama Crimson Tide.betting: Recommendation is Over 8.5 wins, with the case resting almost entirely on quarterback Keelon Russell — and the guide's confidence in Russell resting in turn on DeBoer's quarterback-development record. It advises betting Alabama early, including conference and national championship odds.

Arkansas Razorbacks.previous_hc_experience: A decade at Memphis, where the guide records he won 50 games and four bowls but never won the AAC or even reached its title game. The Coaching Carousel adds that he inherited a good programme and a NIL budget filled by FedEx there.
Arkansas Razorbacks.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Arkansas Razorbacks.dc_status: New — the guide calls Rob Roberts the new coordinator, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Arkansas Razorbacks.qb_development: Asserted at the level of background rather than record: the guide says Silverfield's offensive background should help quarterback KJ Jackson develop.
Arkansas Razorbacks.continuity: None. Head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback all change — the Stability Score table awards zero points on all four.
Arkansas Razorbacks.staff_turnover: Complete at the senior level. Sam Pittman was dismissed in September and the programme finished bottom of the SEC.
Arkansas Razorbacks.prior_school: Memphis. Sutton Smith and receiver Jamari Hawkins (38 receptions, 623 yards) followed Silverfield from Memphis, as did quarterback challenger AJ Hill.
Arkansas Razorbacks.portal_recruiting: The guide records that production drained out of Fayetteville as usually follows a firing — Arkansas lost its leading rusher and top three receivers — and that the staff replaced it with a mix of Memphis followers and other transfers, with the pecking order unknown.
Arkansas Razorbacks.vsin_assessment: Two-sided. The team page casts Silverfield as the programme builder Arkansas needs while noting he never won the AAC. The Coaching Carousel is blunter, calling him seemingly the bronze medalist behind Jon Sumrall and Alex Golesh, and noting the irony that Arkansas went from one offensive-line coach in Sam Pittman to another.
Arkansas Razorbacks.strengths: A decade of head-coaching experience with 50 wins and four bowls, an offensive background the guide expects to help the quarterback, and existing Memphis relationships that brought players with him.
Arkansas Razorbacks.concerns: He never won his previous conference despite good resources, and the guide expects the defense and the SEC schedule to sink the season regardless.
Arkansas Razorbacks.betting: Recommendation is Under 4.5 wins. The coaching change is not the stated reason — the guide expects decent offensive production from Silverfield's background — but the defense and schedule are.
Arkansas Razorbacks.carousel_summary: The guide places the hire in context of the market for coaches: after a decade at Memphis, Silverfield took what it calls probably the only SEC opportunity he was ever going to get. It says it would be unfair to call him the last person at the bar when the lights came on, while stating AD Hunter Yurachek had two strikes in the count and had to put a ball in play. It rates him the bronze medalist behind Sumrall and Golesh and explains why: he inherited a good programme and a FedEx-backed NIL budget at Memphis and never won the conference. It closes on the pattern that Arkansas replaced one offensive-line coach with another, chasing only its second ranked finish since 2011.

Auburn Tigers.previous_hc_experience: First head-coaching job was South Florida, where he went 23-15 before taking Auburn. Before that, four seasons under Matt Campbell and three under Josh Heupel.
Auburn Tigers.dc: DJ Durkin, with Tim Banks also named on the defensive staff.
Auburn Tigers.oc_status: New — Gordon arrives with Golesh from South Florida, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Auburn Tigers.dc_status: Returning — the guide calls retaining Durkin a savvy move, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Auburn Tigers.play_caller: Not addressed in guide as a named role, though the guide notes continuity at play-caller on defense could help the team beat expectations.
Auburn Tigers.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide records that Golesh brought essentially his whole South Florida offense with him, so the system is the one he ran there.
Auburn Tigers.qb_development: Not addressed as a development record. The guide's point is continuity rather than development: Byrum Brown played for Golesh his entire career.
Auburn Tigers.continuity: Unusually high on offense for a first-year head coach, and retained on defense. Coordinator Joel Gordon has worked under Golesh for three years; DJ Durkin stays as defensive coordinator.
Auburn Tigers.staff_turnover: Wholesale on offense but by design — the guide's framing is that Golesh brought his South Florida offense intact rather than rebuilding one.
Auburn Tigers.prior_school: South Florida. Golesh brought coordinator Joel Gordon, quarterback Byrum Brown and six USF receivers, including Jeremiah Koger (38 receptions, 597 yards) and Keshaun Singleton (50 receptions, 877 yards).
Auburn Tigers.portal_recruiting: The staff move is itself the portal story: the guide's question is framed as whether the transferred South Florida offense translates up a level, and it notes Golesh's first-year success will be contingent on how the USF transfers adapt to Power Four life.
Auburn Tigers.vsin_assessment: Positive and specific. The Coaching Carousel explains what Auburn was thinking — the Tigers scored just 18.5 and 19.1 PPG against SEC opponents over the last two seasons — and notes Golesh is an offensive coach through and through who has found points pretty much everywhere he has been. The team page says he inherits close to an ideal situation.
Auburn Tigers.strengths: An offensive specialist inheriting one of the country's best quarterbacks and skill-position talent already familiar with the system, with the defense left in veteran hands.
Auburn Tigers.concerns: The guide's caution is about level rather than method: last season's USF team is taking on an SEC schedule, which it says could be a Year 1 disaster.
Auburn Tigers.betting: Recommendation is Over 6.5 wins, argued from the coaching situation itself — Golesh inherits close to an ideal setup, and he and Brown have already shown they can pull a big upset.
Auburn Tigers.carousel_summary: The guide explains the hire's logic through Auburn's scoring problem — 18.5 and 19.1 PPG against SEC opponents over two seasons — and Golesh's profile as an offensive coach who has spent his entire collegiate career on that side of the ball. It traces the path: four seasons under Matt Campbell, three under Josh Heupel, then 23-15 in his first head-coaching job at South Florida. With the defense in the hands of veterans DJ Durkin and Tim Banks, it says Golesh's chief objective is to find points, something he has done pretty much everywhere. Its stated condition is how the USF transfers adapt to Power Four life, quarterback Byrum Brown included.

Florida Gators.previous_hc_experience: Two seasons as head coach at Troy and two at Tulane, having taken Troy from 15-20 over three seasons to 23-5 with two Sun Belt titles and reached the CFP with Tulane. The Coaching Carousel adds he has won at least 11 games in three of his four seasons as a head coach, and distinguishes the two jobs: he inherited a mess at Troy from Chip Lindsey and a strong foundation at Tulane thanks to Willie Fritz.
Florida Gators.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator. The Georgia Tech spread (p. 91) records Faulkner leaving that programme for Florida.
Florida Gators.dc_status: New — the guide records Sumrall hired Brad White, previously in the same role under Mike Stoops at Kentucky, and the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Florida Gators.qb_development: Not addressed as a record. The guide's stated priority for Aaron Philo is ball security, and it notes Philo played under Faulkner at Georgia Tech for two years.
Florida Gators.continuity: None at the top, but a pre-existing coordinator-to-quarterback relationship: Philo played under Faulkner for two years at Georgia Tech and was recruited by Sumrall.
Florida Gators.staff_turnover: Complete at the senior level — head coach, offensive coordinator and defensive coordinator all new, with the Stability Score table awarding zero points on all three.
Florida Gators.prior_school: Georgia Tech supplies both the offensive coordinator and the expected starting quarterback; Kentucky supplies the defensive coordinator, where Brad White held the same role under Mike Stoops.
Florida Gators.portal_recruiting: Aaron Philo transferred from Georgia Tech, recruited by Sumrall, following his coordinator.
Florida Gators.vsin_assessment: Respectful but sceptical about the leap. The guide has no doubt Sumrall can build a programme, then treats the SEC as a leap many have failed. The Coaching Carousel places Florida between the two jobs he has had — a mess at Troy, a strong foundation at Tulane — and says we will see how long it takes him to bring the Gators back to relevance.
Florida Gators.strengths: A head coach who has known nothing but success across four seasons, entering a fifth straight chase for a conference title game, plus a coordinator who already knows the expected starting quarterback.
Florida Gators.concerns: The guide's reasoning is that Sumrall's streak of conference title games at new programmes has to end somewhere, and that the SEC has defeated many similar rises.
Florida Gators.betting: Recommendation is Under 7.5 wins, argued directly from the coaching situation: the streak has to end somewhere, and while Sumrall has the pieces to get Florida bowling, eight or more wins looks hard.
Florida Gators.carousel_summary: The guide reads Sumrall's rise as increasingly typical of the modern game and traces it in full: four playing years at Kentucky, a graduate assistantship there in 2005-06, an FCS job at San Diego in his mid-20s, then up the ranks to co-defensive coordinator at Kentucky, two seasons as head coach at Troy and two at Tulane. It notes immediate success adds commas to a bank account in college football, with a CFP appearance in 2024 and at least 11 wins in three of four seasons. Its analytical point is about inheritance — a mess at Troy, a strong foundation at Tulane — and it places Florida somewhere in between.

Georgia Bulldogs.oc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Georgia Bulldogs.dc_status: Returning — the Stability Score table (p. 42) awards 3 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Georgia Bulldogs.run_pass: Not addressed as a stated tendency. The guide records the offense was inefficient on the ground — 32nd percentile in explosive run rate and 54th percentile in early-down success — leaving the quarterback to rescue long third downs, which it calls unsustainable.
Georgia Bulldogs.continuity: Complete. Head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback all return — the only SEC programme in this batch to score points on all four Stability components, for a total of 17.
Georgia Bulldogs.portal_recruiting: Kirby Smart signed Auburn transfer Amaris Williams to address the pass rush, but Williams tore an ACL in spring.
Georgia Bulldogs.vsin_assessment: The guide says Smart has work to do on a defense that disappointed in 2025, and leans on his track record to expect it fixed.
Georgia Bulldogs.strengths: Total staff and quarterback continuity behind 14 returning starters from a 12-win team, which the guide reads as enough to go for a third straight SEC title.
Georgia Bulldogs.concerns: The 2025 pass defense. The guide argues the front seven rather than the secondary was the likelier culprit — just 20 sacks and persistent trouble pressuring quarterbacks — and insists improvement must be dramatic for national success.
Georgia Bulldogs.betting: Recommendation is Over 9.5 wins, with the guide openly noting the pricing makes the best wager hard to isolate. The coaching element is its expectation that Smart fixes the defense on his record.

Kentucky Wildcats.previous_hc_experience: None as a head coach — the guide notes he is the second-youngest Power Four head coach, arriving at 36 from three seasons under Dan Lanning at Oregon.
Kentucky Wildcats.oc: Not addressed in guide as a separate appointment; Stein arrives as the offensive mind, having called plays at Oregon.
Kentucky Wildcats.oc_status: New — the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning offensive coordinator.
Kentucky Wildcats.dc_status: New — Jay Bateman arrives from Texas A&M, and the Stability Score table (p. 43) awards 0 points for a returning defensive coordinator.
Kentucky Wildcats.play_caller: Not addressed in guide for 2026. The guide records Stein called plays for Oregon's offense and lists as an open unknown whether he can keep developing quarterbacks while carrying head-coaching duties.
Kentucky Wildcats.offensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide's framing is that Kentucky needs to modernize offensively and that a more dynamic offense will be required to contend in the SEC.
Kentucky Wildcats.defensive_scheme: Not addressed in guide as a named scheme. The guide places Bateman in the Mike Elko tree and says that if he shows Elko-like qualities as a play-caller the unit should at least match 2025.
Kentucky Wildcats.run_pass: Not addressed as a 2026 tendency. The guide characterizes the Mark Stoops era as a tenacious defense with a ball-control offense.
Kentucky Wildcats.qb_development: Explicitly credited. Stein had a hand in developing Bo Nix, Dillon Gabriel and Dante Moore at Oregon and called plays for an offense that never finished below 13th nationally in scoring. The guide rates the fit with Kenny Minchey very highly.
Kentucky Wildcats.continuity: None. Head coach, offensive coordinator, defensive coordinator and quarterback all change — the Stability Score table awards zero on all four for a total of 2.
Kentucky Wildcats.staff_turnover: Complete at the senior level, and by design: the guide describes Stein as the opposite of Stoops in almost every way.
Kentucky Wildcats.prior_school: Oregon, where Stein spent three seasons under Dan Lanning; Texas A&M, where Bateman comes from out of the Elko tree.
Kentucky Wildcats.portal_recruiting: The guide notes Kentucky appears to be spending more to back Stein, records that Minchey was flipped from a Nebraska commitment in a single day with NIL gestured at as the mechanism, and counts six defensive transfers joining Bateman's group.
Kentucky Wildcats.vsin_assessment: Positive on both hires. The Coaching Carousel says it really likes this hire, especially paired with a strong defensive coordinator grab in Bateman, and credits the athletic department for recognising the programme needs to modernize offensively. It supplies a cautionary precedent in the same breath: former Lanning coordinator Kenny Dillingham has done well at Arizona State, but the Sun Devils went 3-9 in his first season as he tore the team down to the studs.
Kentucky Wildcats.strengths: A quarterback developer with a top-13 scoring offense on his record, paired with a defensive coordinator from a respected tree, at a programme the guide says is now spending to support them.
Kentucky Wildcats.concerns: Stated plainly as two unknowns: whether Stein can keep developing quarterbacks while carrying head-coaching duties, and whether he can run an efficient SEC offense with less talent than at Oregon. The guide notes its answer rests on his confidence rather than evidence.
Kentucky Wildcats.betting: Recommendation is Over 4.5 wins, framed explicitly as a statement of belief in Stein's offensive ability, and dependent as well on Bateman getting the defense to repeat its 2025 production.
Kentucky Wildcats.carousel_summary: The guide states its own approval directly — it really likes the hire, especially paired with the Bateman appointment. It identifies Stein as the mastermind of the Oregon offense over three seasons, a Louisville native who played quarterback there from 2008-12, and credits the Kentucky athletic department for recognising the programme must modernize offensively. It is fair to the predecessor: what Mark Stoops did, including eight straight bowls from 2016-23, was very impressive with a tenacious defense and ball-control offense — but the guide argues a more dynamic offense is required to contend in the SEC. Its closing caution is a precedent rather than a doubt: Kenny Dillingham, another former Lanning coordinator, has done well at Arizona State, but went 3-9 in his first season while tearing the team down to the studs.
